title: Grade 9 English Placement
source: Gold Book student reading and language arts diagnostic

questions.subject: english
questions.advisor_key: Civil War camp at dawn/early spring: fogs lifting, muddy roads becoming thoroughfares, an army on the hills, a river, enemy campfires across the water. From The Red Badge of Courage.
questions.stem:
Reading · from The Red Badge of Courage by Stephen Crane

The cold passed reluctantly from the earth, and the retiring fogs revealed an army stretched out on the hills, resting. As the landscape changed from brown to green, the army awakened, and began to tremble with eagerness at the noise of rumors. It cast its eyes upon the roads, which were growing from long troughs of liquid mud to proper thoroughfares. A river, amber-tinted in the shadow of its banks, purled at the army’s feet; and at night, when the stream had become of a sorrowful blackness, one could see across it the red eyelike gleam of hostile camp fires set in the low brows of distant hills.

Once a certain tall soldier developed virtues and went resolutely to wash a shirt. He came flying back from a brook waving his garment bannerlike. He was swelled with a tale he had heard from a reliable friend, who had heard it from a truthful cavalryman, who had heard it from his trustworthy brother, one of the orderlies at division headquarters. He adopted the important air of a herald in red and gold.

1. Explain the setting of this story.

questions.subject: english
questions.advisor_key: A tall soldier goes to wash a shirt, then rushes back waving it like a banner, swollen with a rumor passed through several 'reliable' sources, and acts like a herald in red and gold.
questions.stem:
Reading · same passage

Use the Crane passage from question 1.

2. Describe the soldier and his actions.

questions.subject: english
questions.advisor_key: The Railway Express truck rumbled up Wilson Road and stopped before a new Cape Cod cottage. It was a gray-shingled house with green blinds nestled atop a gently rising slope. The driver of the truck climbed out and began unloading a number of heavy cartons. Mr. Robert Jones, who had a summer house down the road, stood watching with little interest.

questions.subject: english
questions.advisor_key: Correct quotation marks, commas, and speaker tags. Sample: “So when Tegid finished, I stood,” my people I said… Reconstruct the Gold Book dialogue with standard American dialogue punctuation.
questions.stem:
6. Rewrite the passage, adding the correct punctuation for dialogue.

So when Tegid finished, I stood my people I said I welcome you
What is it I whispered to Tegid, who had joined me
They fear your hand I think he replied
Well do something Tell them I bring them peace and goodwill I replied Make them understand

questions.subject: english
questions.advisor_key: a. cautiously → advanced; b. humbly → answered; c. very → severe; very → heavy; (very) frequent. List adverb and the word it modifies.
questions.stem:
7. Name each adverb and the word it modifies. (On paper you would underline and draw an arrow.)

  1. They advanced cautiously into the forest.
  2. He answered humbly, observing that he had been doing his duty.
  3. The winter set in very severe, and the falls of snow were very heavy and frequent.

questions.subject: english
questions.advisor_key: a. lying; b. set; c. lay (put down the book); d. well; e. badly.
questions.stem:
8. Choose the correct word in each sentence. Write the letter and the word you picked.

  1. His socks were (lying, laying) on the floor.
  2. Please don’t (sit, set) your glass on the table.
  3. She could not (lay, lie) down the book.
  4. Sam could write (well, good).
  5. Henry played his piano (bad, badly) at the audition.

questions.advisor_key: a. sat — IT, no DO; b. cracked — T, shells; c. judge — T, book (never judge a book).

10. For each sentence, name the verb, label it transitive (T) or intransitive (IT), and list the direct object if there is one.

  1. The bird sat on her nest.
  2. The hatching ducklings cracked their shells.
  3. You should never judge a book by its cover.

questions.subject: english
questions.advisor_key: Accurate copy of the Black Arrow paragraph, then: subjects/verbs identified, adjectives and adverbs named, prepositional phrases listed, conjunctions named. Partial credit for a faithful copy even if markup is thin.
questions.stem:
11. Copy this paragraph from The Black Arrow. Then mark it in your typed answer: subject of each sentence; verb or verb phrase; adjectives and adverbs; prepositional phrases; conjunctions.

Dick led the way upstairs and along the corridor. In the brown chamber the rope had been made fast to the frame of an exceedingly heavy and ancient bed. It had not been detached, and Dick, taking the coil to the window, began to lower it slowly and cautiously into the darkness of the night. Joan stood by.

Type the copy, then list subjects, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, prepositional phrases, and conjunctions in your answer.
